newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF minister says watching moves in Tokyo stocks.
newsitem.headline: MOF minister says watching moves in Tokyo stocks.

text.p: Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Friday he would like to keep a careful watch over movements in the Tokyo stock market.
"I have and will refrain from commenting on the stock market. Markets move according to market principles. I would like to keep careful watch over the market," he said.

He made the comments after being asked if the stock market's fall and the weakness of the yen against the dollar were due to disappointment in the markets about government plans for financial reform and measures to cut the budget deficit.

Mitsuzuka said the public needed to look at the overall picture and not concentrate on parts that had received severe criticism. He said the government had decided to end income tax cuts and raise the consumption tax to make up for previous tax cuts and in line with a decision made by parliament.

If the government had not taken these decisions on taxes, it would have had to issue more deficit-financing bonds "to make ends meet", which would have made Japan's fiscal deficit the worst among industrialised nations, he said.
He added that massive issues of deficit-financing bonds could lead to inflation.
Mitsuzuka said cabinet ministers agreed on Friday to set up a group to prepare bills for setting up an agency to take over MOF's inspection and supervision functions over the financial industry.

The group, which would probably be made up of various ministry officials, would be set up under the Prime Minister's Office and would aim to submit the bills to the parliament session starting in January.
